# Gene modules with hdWGCNA

This script identifies co-expression modules in the astrocytes with hdWGCNA, the high-dimensional version of WGCNA for single-cell data. Because single-nuclei data is sparse, hdWGCNA first aggregates similar cells into *metacells*, then builds a co-expression network on them, and finally assigns genes to modules. The modules are examined (hub genes, module eigengenes on the UMAP) and annotated with GO terms.

## Defining variables

This code block defines variables to be used throughout the rest of the document. Users can adapt these if desired.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-04-defining-variables

# Input: clustered astrocyte Seurat object (made in 02_clustering.qmd)
file_seurat <- "seu_shortread_astros_clustered.rds"

# Seurat metadata column with the sample ID
col_sample <- "AnonymousID"

# Reductions in the Seurat object
reduction_harmony <- "harmony" # used to find similar cells for metacells
reduction_umap <- "umap"    # used to plot module eigengenes

# hdWGCNA settings
wgcna_name <- "wgcna"      # name of the hdWGCNA experiment in the object
gene_fraction <- 0.05      # keep genes expressed in at least 5% of cells
k_metacells <- 25          # number of cells aggregated per metacell (default)
network_type <- "signed"
soft_power <- 12           # lowest power with SFT model fit >= 0.8 (see
                           # fig-01-soft-powers; [CHECK] re-check this if the
                           # input object or settings change!)
module_prefix <- "AST-M"   # modules are renamed to AST-M1, AST-M2, ...
n_hubs <- 10               # hub genes to extract per module
seed <- 42                 # metacell construction is random, so I set a seed

```

### theme_quarto() and theme_manuscript()

I created my own themes to add to figures. `theme_quarto()` is used to add themes to figures as displayed in the Quarto document and saved to disk as `.pdf` or `.png`. `theme_manuscript()` is used to add themes to figures as they will end up in the manuscript.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-06-helper-themes
theme_quarto <- function(
    legend_position = "right", 
    plot_title = element_blank()
    ) {
    theme(
      plot.title = plot_title,
      legend.position = legend_position
    )
}

theme_manuscript <- function(
    legend_position = "none",
    plot_title = element_blank(),
    axis_title_size = 8,
    axis_text_size = 6
    ) {
    theme(
      plot.title = plot_title,
      legend.position = legend_position,
      axis.title = element_text(size = axis_title_size),
      axis.text = element_text(size = axis_text_size),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"), 
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 9)
    )
}

```

### save_plot()

This document displays all the figures I make, but I also want them saved to disk — both as `.png` and `.pdf`. I only need to provide the ggplot object, a filename (without extension), and optionally the width and height of the figure.

The figures for my written report contain subfigures spread across multiple scripts. Since I want to assemble these panel figures via R code rather than by hand, `save_plot()` can also optionally save the plot object itself to disk as an .rds file, for a final script to later combine with `patchwork`. Set figure to the name the figure should carry in the report (e.g. `"SF1A"`) to trigger this; leave it `NULL` (the default) to just save the `.png`/`.pdf` as normal.

A live ggplot object carries its underlying data along with it — for plots built from large Seurat objects, this can balloon the saved file to gigabytes. To avoid this, `save_plot()` converts the object to a grob (a static, pre-rendered drawing, with no data attached) before saving it as `.rds`. This is controlled by the `grob` argument, and defaults to `TRUE`, since converting a small plot costs nothing but forgetting to convert a large one is expensive. Set `grob = FALSE` only if a later step specifically needs the original, live ggplot object rather than its rendered form.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-05-helper-save-plot
save_plot <- function(
    p, filename, 
    width = 10, height = 6, 
    figure = NULL, grob = TRUE, apply_theme = TRUE, 
    add_tag = TRUE, tag_text_size = 14,
    legend_pos_manuscript = "none"
    ) {
  ## Save image on disk as png and pdf
  # Add Quarto-specific theme, unless the plot has its own custom theme
  if (apply_theme) {
    p_image <- p + theme_quarto()
  } else {
    p_image <- p
  }
  file_png <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".png"))
  ggsave(file_png, p_image, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
  file_pdf <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".pdf"))
  ggsave(file_pdf, p_image, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
  
  ## Save the ggplot object on disk as an rds file 
  if (!is.null(figure)) {
    # Add tag if needed
    if (add_tag) {
      tag <- str_extract(figure, "[A-Z]$")
      p <- p + 
        labs(tag = tag) + 
        theme(
          plot.tag = element_text(
            face = "bold", 
            size = tag_text_size, 
            hjust = 0, vjust = 0
            )
        )
    }
    # Add manuscript-specific theme, unless the plot has its own custom theme
    if (apply_theme) {
      p <- p + theme_manuscript(legend_pos_manuscript)
    }
    file_rds <- file.path(dir_man, paste0(figure, ".rds"))
    # Convert the object to a grob if needed
    if (grob) {
      p <- ggplotGrob(p)
    }
    # Save on disk
    saveRDS(p, file_rds)
  }
}
```

# Preparing the Seurat object

I load the clustered astrocyte Seurat object from disk.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-07-load-seurat
seu <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data, file_seurat))
```

In the .R script, I ran `UpdateSeuratObject()` because I thought hdWGCNA requires Seurat v4, whereas my object is v5.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-08-update-seurat
# [CHECK] My old comment said this "converted Seurat to v5", but the object was
# already v5, and UpdateSeuratObject() updates *older* objects to the current
# version. So what did this line actually do? Check the hdWGCNA documentation
# for which Seurat versions it supports, and check class/version of the object
# (e.g. packageVersion("Seurat"), snrna_astros@version). If the line does
# nothing, remove it and this paragraph.
seu <- SeuratObject::UpdateSeuratObject(seu)
```

# hdWGCNA preprocessing

## Selecting genes

I select genes by fraction, as I only want to include genes expressed in at least 5% of cells (as defined under the header "Define Variables".

```{r}
#| label: chunk-09-setup-wgcna
seu <- SetupForWGCNA(
  seu,
  gene_select = "fraction",
  fraction = gene_fraction,
  wgcna_name = wgcna_name # stored as the name of the hdWGCNA experiment
)
```

## Constructing metacells

Metacells are constructed in each group. Normally, one groups by sample and cell type, but as all cells are astrocytes, I only group by sample (`AnonymousID`).

```{r}
#| label: chunk-10-metacells
# Metacell construction is stochastic, so I set a seed (for reproducibility)
set.seed(seed)

seu <- MetacellsByGroups(
  seurat_obj = seu,
  group.by = col_sample,
  ident.group = col_sample,
  reduction = reduction_harmony,
  k = k_metacells
)

# Normalize metacell expression matrix
seu <- NormalizeMetacells(seu)
```

## Setting the expression matrix

I make sure the right assay and layer are used. This should be the default, but I specify `RNA` and `data` to be sure.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-11-set-datexpr
seu <- SetDatExpr(
  seu,
  assay = "RNA",
  layer = "data"
)
```

# Selecting the soft power threshold

The soft power threshold is extremely important in WGCNA: it acts as a Boolean-like threshold separating strong from weak connections in the correlation matrix, a step essential to reduce noise. `TestSoftPowers()` runs a parameter sweep. One should pick the lowest soft power with a scale-free topology (SFT) model fit greater than or equal to 0.8. In my case, that was at 12, so I set that as the threshold (defined in the section "Define Variables")

```{r}
#| label: chunk-12-test-soft-powers
seu <- TestSoftPowers(
  seu,
  networkType = network_type
)

plot_list_powers <- PlotSoftPowers(seu)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-01-soft-powers
#| fig-cap: "Parameter sweep of soft power thresholds: scale-free topology model fit and mean connectivity per power."
p_soft_powers <- wrap_plots(plot_list_powers, ncol = 2)
p_soft_powers
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-13-save-soft-powers
#| echo: false
ggsave(file.path(dir_fig, "hdwgcna_softpowersplot.png"), p_soft_powers,
       width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 150)
```

I also save the results as a table so I can inspect the exact numbers. The soft power I chose (`soft_power`, defined at the top) is the lowest power with an SFT model fit of at least 0.8.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-14-power-table
power_table <- GetPowerTable(seu)
write_csv(power_table, file.path(dir_tab, "power_table.csv"))
kable(power_table)
```

# Constructing the co-expression network

```{r}
#| label: chunk-15-construct-network
seu <- ConstructNetwork(
  seu,
  soft_power = soft_power, # selected based on TestSoftPowers()
  tom_name = "hdwgcna_astros",
  tom_outdir = dir_tom
)
```

The network is visualized with a dendrogram. `PlotDendrogram()` uses a WGCNA function that predates ggplot2, so it does not return a ggplot object and needs a different way of saving to disk.

```{r}
#| label: fig-02-dendrogram
#| fig-cap: "Dendrogram of the astrocyte co-expression network, with genes coloured by module."
PlotDendrogram(seu, main = "Astros hdWGCNA Dendrogram")
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-16-save-dendrogram
#| echo: false
png(file.path(dir_fig, "hdwgcna_dendrogram.png"), 
    width = 1200, height = 800, res = 150)
PlotDendrogram(seu, main = "Astros hdWGCNA Dendrogram")
dev.off()
```

# Module eigengenes and connectivity

## Module eigengenes

Module eigengenes summarize the expression of each module per cell. I harmonize them by sample.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-17-eigengenes
seu <- ModuleEigengenes(
  seu,
  group.by.vars = col_sample
)

# Extract harmonized module eigengenes
eigengenes <- GetMEs(seu)
```

## Module connectivity

I compute the eigengene-based connectivity (kME) of each gene to each module, and rename the modules.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-18-connectivity
seu <- ModuleConnectivity(seu)

seu <- ResetModuleNames(
  seu,
  new_name = module_prefix
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-03-kme-ranked
#| fig-cap: "Genes ranked by kME for each module."
# [CHECK] In the .R script I used png() for this plot. I believe PlotKMEs()
# returns a patchwork/ggplot object, so it should display directly. Verify; if
# it does not, go back to the png()/dev.off() approach of chunk-16.
p_kme <- PlotKMEs(seu, ncol = 5)
p_kme
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-19-save-kme
#| echo: false
ggsave(file.path(dir_fig, "hdwgcna_kme_genes_ranked.png"), p_kme,
       width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 150)
```

# Extracting hub genes and module assignments

Hub genes are the genes with the highest kME in each module.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-20-hub-genes
hub_df <- GetHubGenes(seu, n_hubs = n_hubs)
write_csv(hub_df, file.path(dir_tab, "hub_genes.csv"))
kable(head(hub_df, 10))
```

The module assignment table links each gene to its module.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-21-module-table
modules <- GetModules(seu)
write_csv(modules, file.path(dir_tab, "module_assignment_table.csv"))
table(modules$module)
```

# Visualizing module eigengenes on the UMAP

A feature plot of the harmonized module eigengenes (hMEs) for each module, ordered so cells with the highest hMEs are plotted on top.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-22-module-feature-plots
plot_list_mes <- ModuleFeaturePlot(
  seu,
  reduction = reduction_umap,
  features = "hMEs", # plot the hMEs
  order = TRUE # order so the points with highest hMEs are on top
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-04-module-feature-plot
#| fig-cap: "Harmonized module eigengenes (hMEs) of each module on the astrocyte UMAP."
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 8
# [CHANGE] Adjust ncol/size to the number of modules you actually found
p_module_features <- wrap_plots(plot_list_mes, ncol = 6)
p_module_features
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-23-save-module-features
#| echo: false
ggsave(file.path(dir_fig, "hdwgcna_module_feature_plot.png"),
       p_module_features, width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 150)
```

3. Add narrative text and new chunks (chunk-25-..., fig-05-...) here. -->

```{r}
#| label: chunk-xx-go-terms
#| eval: false
# First load in the gene set using msigdbr::msigdbr()
gs_go_bp <- msigdbr(
  species = "Homo sapiens", 
  collection = "C5", 
  subcollection = "GO:BP"
)
# Adapt the gene set to the input required for fgsea: it needs to be a list 
# with your pathways/gene set names and the genes that make up each pathway.
gene_sets <- split(x = gs_go_bp$gene_symbol, f = gs_go_bp$gs_name)

# Get the modules table and remove grey genes
modules <- GetModules(seu) %>% subset(module != 'grey')

# rank all genes in this kME - I took this directly from the hdWGCNA fgsea
# vignette
cur_mod <- 'AST-M5'
cur_genes <- modules[,(c('gene_name', 'module', paste0('kME_', cur_mod)))]
gene_scores <- cur_genes$kME
names(gene_scores) <- cur_genes$gene_name
gene_scores <- ranks[order(gene_scores)]

gsea_res <- fgsea(
    pathways = gene_sets, # List of gene sets to check
    stats = gene_scores,
    scoreType = 'std', # std as we have both pos and neg rankings
    minSize = 10, # otherwise I only get pathways with 2-5 genes
    maxSize = 500,
  )

# Decide how many plots you want to make for the upregulated and downregulated
# genes
number_of_top_pathways_down <- 10
number_of_top_pathways_up <- -10


gsea_pathway_selection <- function(gsea_results, n_up = 10, n_down = 0) {
  top_pathways_up <- gsea_results |> 
    filter(padj < 0.05) |>  
    slice_max(NES, n = n_up) |>
    pull(pathway)
  top_pathways_down <- gsea_results |>
    filter(padj < 0.05) |>
    slice_min(NES, n = n_down) |>
    pull(pathway)
  top_pathways <- c(top_pathways_up, rev(top_pathways_down))
  top_pathways
}

## Create a visualization - still need to transfer this function
top_pathways <- gsea_pathway_selection(
  gsea_res, 
  n_up = number_of_top_pathways_up,
  n_down = number_of_top_pathways_down
  )
p_gsea <- plotGseaTable(
  gene_sets[top_pathways], 
  stats = gene_scores, 
  fgseaRes = gsea_res, 
  pathwayLabelStyle = list(size = 9),
  gseaParam = 0.5 # Makes the figure clearer
  )



```
